73:1: What he means by his saying O you wrapped in your garments is the one wrapped in his garments, and what he meant by that is the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The commentators differed regarding the meaning with which God described His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in this verse, regarding covering himself. Some of them said: He described him as being wrapped in his clothes, preparing for prayer. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: O you who is wrapped in your garments: meaning the one wrapped in his garments. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Qatada: O you who is wrapped in your garments means the one who is wrapped in his garments. Others said: He described him as being clothed in prophecy and the message. Who said that? Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Abd Al-A’la told us, he said: Dawud told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding His statement, O you who are wrapped up in clothing, arise and pray the night, except for a little, he said: Wrap yourself in this matter, so perform it. Abu Ja`far said: What is more correct of the two interpretations of this is what Qatada said, because he followed it with his saying, Stand up at night, which was a clarification of his description of him wearing clothes for prayer, and that this is the more apparent of its two meanings.
73:2: And his saying: Stand up all night, except for a little means he is saying to his Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Stand up all night, O Muhammad, except for a little of it.
73:3: Half of it he says: Stand up half of the night or reduce it a little.
73:4: Or add to it. He says: Or add to it. God Almighty gave him the choice when He imposed on him the night prayer between these stations. Whichever of them he wanted, he did. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions, as mentioned, would perform the night prayer, similar to their prayer in the month of Ramadan, as mentioned, until it became easier for them. Who said that? Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Abu Usama told us, on the authority of Misa’ar, he said: Samak al-Hanafi told us, he said: I heard Ibn Abbas say: When the beginning of al-Muzzammil was revealed, they would stand for approximately the same amount of time as they stand in Ramadan, and there was nearly a year between its beginning and its end. Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Muhammad bin Bishr told us, on the authority of Mas`ad, he said: Samak told us, that he heard Ibn Abbas say, and he mentioned something similar, except that he said something similar to their standing in the month of Ramadan. Ibn Wakee’ narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Hayyan, on the authority of Musa ibn Ubaydah, who said: Muhammad ibn Tahla’, the freed slave of Umm Salamah, narrated to me, on the authority of Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Aisha, who said: I used to make a mat for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to pray on at night. The people heard about it and gathered around him. He went out looking angry, but he was merciful to them. He feared that the night prayer would be prescribed for them, so he said: “O people, undertake as much work as you can bear, for God does not tire of reward until you tire of work. The best of deeds are those that you continue to do.” And the Qur’an was revealed: “O you who are wrapped up in a cloak, stand [in prayer] during the night, except for a little. Half of it, or subtract a little from it, or add to it.” So a man would tie a rope and hang on. They were able to do that for eight months. Then God saw what they sought of His pleasure, so He had mercy on them, so He returned them to the obligatory prayers and abandoned the night prayer.” “Ibn Humayd narrated to us: Mihran narrated to us, on the authority of Musa ibn Ubaydah al-Himyari, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Tahla’, on the authority of Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Aishah, who said: I used to buy a mat for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he would stand on it at the beginning of the night, so the people would hear his prayer. A group of people gathered, and when he saw their gathering, he disliked it and feared that it would be written down for them. So he entered the house looking angry, and they began to clear their throats and cough until he came out to them and said: O people, God does not get tired until you get tired, meaning of the reward. So do as much work as you can, for the best work is that which is done consistently, even if it is little. And the verse, ‘O you who are wrapped up in a cloak, stand [in prayer] during the night, except for a little…’ was revealed to him. He said: So it was written down for them, and it was revealed as an obligation, so that one of them would tie a rope and cling to it. But when God saw what they were required to do, seeking thereby God’s face and His pleasure, God relieved them, and said: ‘Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand [in prayer] nearly two-thirds of the night or half of it…’… to ‘He knows that you will not…’” He counted them, so He repented to you. He returned them to the obligatory prayers, and removed from them the voluntary prayers, except for what they volunteered. Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, “Stand [in prayer] during the night, except for a little. Half of it, or subtract from it a little, or add to it, and recite the Qur’an with measured recitation.” So God commanded His Prophet and the believers to stand during the night, except for a little. This was difficult for the believers, then He made it easier for them and had mercy on them. And after this, God revealed, He knows that among you will be sick and others traveling throughout the land, to His statement, So recite what is easy for you from it. (al-Muzzammil 73:20) So God expanded, and to Him be praise, and did not make it difficult. Ibn Hamid told us: Ya`qub told us, on the authority of Ja`far, on the authority of Sa`id, who said: When God revealed to His Prophet, O you who is wrapped in garments, he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, remained in this state for ten years, saying, The night, as God commanded him, and a group of his companions would stand with him. Then God revealed to him after ten years, Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand [in prayer] nearly two-thirds of the night, or half of it, or a third of it, and [so do] a group of those with you... until His saying, And establish prayer. So God lightened their burden after ten years. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us on the authority of Al-Hussein, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Ikrimah and Al-Hasan, they said: He said in Surat Al-Muzzammil, “Stand [in prayer] during the night, except for a little. Half of it, or subtract from it a little, or add to it, and recite the Qur’an with measured recitation.” This was abrogated by the verse in which it says, “He knew that you could not count it, so He turned to you in forgiveness. So recite what is easy for you of the Qur’an.” (al-Muzzammil 73:20) Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Stand during the night, except for a little. They stood for a year or two until their shins and feet were swollen. Then God revealed a simplification later at the end of the surah. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Qais bin Wahb, on the authority of Abu Abd al-Rahman, who said: When the verse, O you wrapped in a cloak, was revealed, they stood reciting it for a year until their feet and legs swelled, until the verse, Then recite what is easy for you of it, was revealed, and the people were relieved. He said: Mahran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jarir, the seller of silk, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: Praise be to God, it is a voluntary act after an obligatory act. Abu Kurayb told us: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Mubarak, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: When the verse O you who are wrapped up was revealed, the Muslims stood for a year, some of them able to bear it and some of them not, until the permission was revealed. He said: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When the beginning of Al-Muzzammil was revealed, they used to stand for approximately the same amount of time as they stand in the month of Ramadan, and there was approximately a year between its beginning and its end. And His saying, And recite the Qur’an with measured recitation, God Almighty says: And explain the Qur’an clearly when you recite it, and recite it slowly. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Abu Raja’ told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement, And recite the Qur’an with measured recitation, he said: Recite it with clear recitation. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, And recite the Qur’an with measured recitation, so he said: Some of it following some of it. Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Makhzumi told us: Jaafar bin Awn told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: And recite the Qur’an with measured recitation. He said: Some of it following some of it, slowly. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, And recite the Qur’an with measured recitation, he said: Recite it slowly. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: And recite the Qur’an with measured recitation. He said: Some of it following some of it. Zakariya bin Yahya bin Abi Zaida told me, he said: Hajjaj bin Muhammad told us, he said: Ibn Jurayj said, on the authority of Ata’, And recite the Qur’an with measured recitation. He said: Recitation means throwing away, casting away. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And recite the Qur’an with measured recitation. He said: Explain it clearly. Abu Kurayb told us: Waki` told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Layla, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And recite the Qur’an with measured recitation. He said: Explain it clearly. Abu Kurayb told us: Waki` told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: And recite the Qur’an with measured recitation. He said: Some of it after some.
73:5: The people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of His statement: Indeed, We will cast upon you a weighty word. Some of them said: What he meant by it is that We will cast upon you a weighty word that must be acted upon. Who said that? Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding His statement, Indeed, We will cast upon you a weighty word, he said: Acting upon it. He said: A man may recite the surah, but acting upon it is heavy. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: Indeed, We will cast upon you a weighty word. God’s obligations and limits are heavy. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: Heavy, he said: God’s obligations and limits are heavy. Others said: Rather, he meant by that that the statement itself is heavy to bear. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, that when revelation came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was on his camel, it would lower its hump and would not be able to move until it was removed from him. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding the statement of God: Indeed, We will cast upon you a weighty word, he said: By God, it is a heavy and blessed Qur’an, just as it was heavy in this world, it will be heavy on the scales on the Day of Resurrection. The most correct statement on this matter is to say: God described it as a heavy statement, so just as Muhammad described it as heavy, he is heavy in working with its limits and obligations.
73:6: And His saying: Indeed, the rising of the night is most severe in its impact. The Almighty and Majestic means by His saying: Indeed, the rising of al-Layl 92:that the hours of the night, and every hour of the hours of the night is rising from the night. The interpreters differed on this: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Hatim ibn Abi Saghira told us, he said: I said to Abdullah ibn Abi Malekah: Will you not tell me which part of the night is the rising? He said: It has been omitted from the verse. I asked Ibn Abbas about it, and he claimed that the whole night is the rising. I asked Ibn al-Zubayr about it, and he told me the same. Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Hakam told us, he said: Anbasa told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Indeed, the one who rises at night he said: In the language of the Abyssinians, when a man rises at night, they say: he rose. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Indeed, the one who rises at night rises means he rises. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Maysarah, Indeed, the rising of the night, he said: rising means getting up. He said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, he said: If a man gets up at night, then he is the one who rises at night. Hanad bin Al-Sarri told us: Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement, Indeed, the rising of the night, he said: It is the entire night. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: The rising of the night means: If you get up at night, then it is the rising of the night. He said: Mahran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid: Everything after the evening meal is considered a rising meal. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Indeed, the rising of the night, he said: The standing of the night. He said: And at whatever hour of the night he rises, he has risen. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Whatever night you get up for, it is a rising. He said: Mihran told us, on the authority of Kharijah, on the authority of Abu Yunus Hatim bin Abi Saghira, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, who said: I asked Ibn Abbas and Ibn al-Zubayr about the rising of the night, and they said: The whole night is a rising, but if you rise while standing, then that is a rising. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: Indeed, the hours of the night he said: meaning the hour in which one prays at night. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: Indeed, the rising of the night meaning the entire night. Abu Kurayb told us: Waki` told us, on the authority of Abu Amir Al-Khazzaz, and Nafi` told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Indeed, the rising of the night he said: The entire night. He said: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: The whole night, if he stands to pray, is a period of rising. Others said: Rather, that is what happened after dinner, but what happened before dinner is not a new event. Who said that? Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Sulayman al-Taymi, on the authority of Abu Majlaz, regarding his statement: Indeed, the rising of the night he said: What comes after the evening prayer is the rising. He said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Abu Raja’ told us, regarding his statement: Indeed, the night prayer he said: What comes after the last evening prayer. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: Indeed, the rising of the night he said: The rising of al-Layl 92:what comes after the evening prayer is the rising of the night. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Sulayman told us, he said: Abu Hilal told us, he said: Qatada said regarding His statement: Indeed, the rising of the night he said: Everything after the evening prayer is a rising. And his saying: It is more severe in its recitation. The reciters of the regions differed in their recitation of that. The majority of the reciters of Mecca, Medina, and Kufa recited it as more severe in its recitation with a fat-ha on the waw and a sukoon on the ta’. Some of the reciters of Basra, Mecca, and Syria recited it as wata’ with a kasra on the waw and a long alif, as a source from the saying of the speaker: The tongue fell into a covenant with the heart, a covenant and a covenant. The correct thing to say about this, in our view, is that they are two well-known readings with correct meanings, so whichever one the reader recites, he is correct. What he means by his saying: It is more intense is that the night is more steadfast than the day and more firmly established in the heart, because work at night is more firmly established than during the day. It was narrated from the Arabs that they walked at night, meaning they travelled during it. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said that whoever reads it with the opening of the waw and the sukoon of the ta’ said, even though their expressions differed in that regard. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: It is more firm in its adherence: meaning it is more steadfast in goodness and more retentive in memory. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: It is more severe. He said: Standing at night is more severe. He said: It is more steadfast in goodness. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Indeed, the rising of the night is most effective in concurrence meaning: The rising of the night was their prayer at the beginning of the night. It is most effective in concurrence meaning: It is more likely that you will count what God has enjoined upon you of standing, because when a person sleeps, he does not know when he will wake up. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement: Indeed, the rising of the night is most effective for concurrence, he said: Indeed, the one who prays at night and stands in prayer at night is most effective for concurrence: tranquility that frees his heart for it, and that is because he is not confronted by needs or anything. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement: It is more effective, that is, reciting the Qur’an at night is more firmly established than during the day, and more effective at night than during the day. As for those who read wata’ with a kasra on the waw and a long alif, I have mentioned what they meant by their reading as well. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: More severe he said: That you are in agreement with your heart, your hearing, and your sight. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Mujahid: Indeed, the rising of the night is most effective. He said: Your hearing, sight, and heart agree. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: more severe he said: in agreement with the speech, and freeing the heart. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: I heard Ibn Abi Nujayh say about His statement: Indeed, the rising of the night is most effective for concurrence and most suitable for speech, he said: It is more likely to be in agreement with your hearing, to be in agreement with your sight. Ibn Hamid told us: Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: More severe he said: More likely to be in agreement with your hearing and heart. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: Indeed, the rising of the night is most effective for concurrence and most suitable for speech. He said: Your hearing, sight, and speech are in agreement with one another. And his saying: And the most correct reading. He says: And the most correct reading. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Yahya bin Dawud Al-Wasiti told us: Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, who said: Anas recited this verse: Indeed, the rising of the night is most effective for concurrence and most correct for words. Some of the people said to him: O Abu Hamza, it is most correct for words. He said: More correct, “more correct,” and more prepared are one and the same. Musa bin Abdul Rahman Al-Masruqi told me: Abdul Hamid Al-Hammani told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, who said: Anas read and I stand upright and I prepare myself properly. It was said to him, O Abu Hamza, it is actually ‘and I stand upright.’ Anas said: I prepare myself properly, I stand upright, and I prepare myself properly are one and the same. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Abu Kuraib told us: Waki` told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement: And I speak the most upright words means: closer to understanding the Qur’an. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And I am more upright in speech is better at remembering the recitation. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: And I stand up straight, he said: I stand up straight reading for his being free from the world.
73:7: His saying: Indeed, you have a long period of time during the day. God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: O Muhammad, you have a long period of time during the day in which you can relax and move about. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: A long sleep means a long period of time, meaning sleep. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Muammil told us, he said: Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement: Indeed, for you during the day is a prolonged enjoyment. He said: A prolonged enjoyment. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: for a long time, he said: for a long time. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: Indeed, for you during the day is much exertion, he said: For your needs, so devote the night to your religion. They said: This was when the night prayer was obligatory, then God bestowed His favor upon the servants and made it lighter and abolished it, and He recited: Stand [in prayer] during the night, except for a little… to the end of the verse. Then He said: Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand [in prayer] nearly two-thirds of the night (al-Muzzammil 73:20), until He reached His statement: So recite what is easy of it (al-Muzzammil 73:20), the night being half or a third of it. Then a more comprehensive and more expansive command came, abolishing the obligation from Him and his nation, and He said: “And during part of the night, pray with it as an additional prayer for you. Perhaps your Lord will raise you to a station of praise” [al-Isra’ 79]. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say about His statement: Indeed, for you during the day is a prolonged period of time, that it is a long period of time. Yahya bin Ya’mar used to read it with a kha’. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Abdul-Mumin told us, on the authority of Ghalib Al-Laithi, on the authority of Yahya bin Ya`mar from the tribe of Jadhila Qais that he used to recite a long salt marsh. He said: It is sleep. Abu Jaafar said: Tasbikh means spreading out and fluffing up cotton and wool. It is said to a woman: Sabkhi qutnak meaning, spread it out and fluff it up. From this comes the saying of Al-Akhtal: So send them to scatter the dust as one scatters the fluffy cotton strings. What he meant by his saying: Indeed, you have plenty of time during the day is that you have plenty of time during the day to take care of your needs and those of your people. The meaning of swimming and salt water is close in this context.
73:8: God Almighty says: And remember O Muhammad the name of your Lord “and call upon Him by it” and devote yourself to Him with a complete devotion meaning: and devote yourself to Him with a complete devotion for your needs and worship, without all other things besides Him. This is from their saying: I devote myself to this matter, and from this the mother of Jesus, son of Mary, was called the Virgin, because of her devotion to God. And it is said of the worshipper who is cut off from the world and its causes to the worship of God: He has devoted himself to Him, and from this is the report that was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace that he forbade devotion. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And devote yourself to Him with a complete devotion, he said: Be sincere to Him with a complete sincerity. Abu Kuraib told us: Yahya told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And devote yourself to Him with a complete devotion. He said: Be sincere to Him with a complete devotion. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Muammil told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: And devote yourself to Him with a complete devotion. He said: Be sincere to Him with a complete sincerity. Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Mihran told us, he said: Mihran told us on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Abu Kurayb told us: Waki` told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mujahid, the same, except that he said: I will go to him. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: And devote yourself to Him with a complete devotion. He said: Be sincerely devoted to Him. Yaqoub told me, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Abu Yahya Al-Makki, regarding his statement: And devote yourself to Him with a complete devotion, he said: Be sincere to Him with a complete devotion. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And devote yourself to Him with a complete devotion, he said: I devote my request and supplication to Him. Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding His statement: And devote yourself to Him with a complete devotion, he said: Devote yourself and strive. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: And devote yourself to Him with a complete devotion means: devote your worship and supplication to Him sincerely. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, in a similar manner. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement: And devote yourself to Him with a complete devotion, that he said: Be sincere to Him with a complete devotion. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the statement of K, And devote yourself to Him with a complete devotion, he said: That is, devote yourself to His worship. He said: Devote yourself, so how desirable is devotion to God. And he recited the statement of God, So when you have finished, then strive (al-Sharh 94:7), he said: When you have finished with jihad, then devote yourself to the worship of God, And to your Lord turn your longing (al-Sharh 94:8).
73:9: And his saying: Lord of the East and the West. The reciters differed in their recitation of that. The majority of the reciters of Medina recited it in the nominative case as a beginning, since it was the beginning of a verse after another complete one. The majority of the reciters of Kufa recited it in the genitive case as a description and in response to the ha’ in his saying: And devote yourself to Him. The correct thing to say about this, in our view, is that they are two well-known readings, each of which has been recited by scholars among the reciters. So whichever one the reciter recites, he is correct. The meaning of the statement is: Lord of the East and the West and of the world between them. His saying: There is no god but Him means: No god should be worshipped but God, who is the Lord of the East and the West. His saying: Then take him as a trustee in what he commands you and delegate your causes to him.
73:10: And His statement: And be patient over what they say and leave them with gracious leave. God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Be patient, O Muhammad, over what the polytheists among your people say to you, and over their harm, and leave them for the sake of God with gracious leave. Gracious leave is leaving for the sake of God, as God Almighty says: And when you see those who engage in [offensive] discourse concerning Our verses, then turn away from them until they engage in another conversation. (Al-An`am: 68)... the verse. And it was said that this was abrogated. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And be patient over what they say and leave them with gracious leave, Surah Bara’ah abrogated what was here. He commanded that they be fought until they testify that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, and nothing else will be accepted from them.
73:11: He, the Most High, means by His saying: And leave Me and the deniers, so leave Me, O Muhammad, and the deniers of My signs, those of ease, meaning those who are comfortable in this world, and give them respite for a little while, meaning: and delay them with the punishment that I have extended for them for a little while until the Book reaches its term. He mentioned that the period between the revelation of this verse and the Battle of Badr was short. Who said that? Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Ibn Ibad, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibad, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, on the authority of Aisha, who said: When this verse was revealed, “And leave Me and the deniers of wealth and grant them respite for a little. Indeed, with Us are shackles and a blazing Fire”… the verse, he said: It was only a short time before the Battle of Badr occurred. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, God said: And leave Me and the deniers, those of ease, and grant them respite for a little. He said: God has a request and a need for them.
73:12: And His statement: Indeed, with Us are shackles and a Hellfire. God Almighty says: Indeed, with Us for those who deny Our signs are shackles, meaning chains, the singular of which is: shackle. And the people of interpretation said the same as we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Al-Mu’tamir told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Amr, on the authority of Ikrimah: The verse in which he said: Indeed, with Us are shackles and a blazing Fire is shackles. Ubaid bin Asbat bin Muhammad told me: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Abu Amr, on the authority of Ikrimah: Indeed, with Us are shackles. He said: Chains. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Yahya and Abd al-Rahman told us, they said: Sufyan told us, he said: Abu Amr told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, Shackles he said: chains. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Amr, on the authority of Ikrimah, Indeed, with Us are shackles. He said: Chains. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, he said: It was reported to me on the authority of Mujahid that he said: Ankaal: chains. Ibn Hamid told us: Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Hammad, who said: Ankaal means shackles. Muhammad bin Isa Al-Damaghani told me: Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Hammad, the same. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, he said: I heard Hammad say: The shackles are the chains. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Indeed, with Us are shackles: meaning chains. Abu Kurayb told us: Waki` told us, on the authority of Mubarak, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Amr ibn Al-`As, on the authority of `Ikrimah: Indeed, with Us are shackles. He said: Chains. Abu Ubaid Al-Wasabi Muhammad bin Hafs told us, he said: Ibn Hamir told us, he said: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Hammad, regarding his statement, Indeed, with Us are shackles and a blazing Fire, he said: The shackles are the chains. Saeed bin Unbasa Al-Razi told us: I passed by Ibn Al-Sammak while he was narrating and he said: I heard Al-Thawri say: I heard Hammad say about the statement of God, Indeed, with Us are shackles, he said: Black chains from the fire of Hell. And his saying: And Hellfire means: And a blazing fire.
73:13: And food that chokes He says: And food that chokes the eater, so it neither goes down his throat nor comes out of it. As Ishaq bin Wahb and Ibn Sinan Al-Qazzaz told me, they said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Shabib bin Bishr told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And food that chokes, he said: A thorn that takes hold of the throat, so it neither enters nor exits. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And food that chokes, he said: The tree of Zaqqum. His saying: A painful torment means: A painful, hurtful torment. Abu Kurayb told us: Waki` told us, on the authority of Hamza al-Zayyat, on the authority of Hamran bin A`yan, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited, Indeed, with Us are shackles and a blazing Fire, and food that chokes. Then he, may God bless him and grant him peace, was struck dumb.
73:14: God Almighty says: Indeed, We have for these polytheists of Quraysh who harm you, O Muhammad, the punishments that He described on the Day when the earth and mountains will shake. And the shaking of that means its disturbance with those on it, and that is on the Day of Resurrection. And his saying, And the mountains were like a heap of sand, means: And the mountains were like liquid, scattered sand. And mahl is the object of the saying of the speaker: I made the sand heap, so I make it heap, and that is if its bottom is stirred, so it rains down on it from above. And the Arabs have two dialects for that, saying: mahil and mahyul, and makil and makil, and from it the saying of the poet: Your people used to think you were a master, but I think you are a foolish master. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah bin Saleh told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And the mountains will become like poured sand, meaning: liquid sand. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And the mountains will become like heaps of sand. He said: The heaped sand is the soft sand that when you touch it, it rolls down. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, a pouring sand dune, he said: it pours down.
73:15: God Almighty says, Indeed, We have sent to you, O people, a Messenger as a witness over you to answer whoever among you answers My call, and to refrain from answering whoever among you refuses to answer, on the Day you meet Me on the Day of Resurrection just as We sent to Pharaoh a Messenger He says: Just as We sent before you to Pharaoh of Egypt a Messenger to call him to the truth.
73:16: But Pharaoh disobeyed the Messenger whom We sent to him, so We seized him with a terrible punishment. He says: So We seized him with a severe punishment, and destroyed him and all those with him. This is from their saying: unpleasant grass, if it is not enjoyed, and the same applies to food. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, a severe punishment, he said: severe. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, So We seized him with a terrible punishment, meaning severe. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, So We seized him with a terrible punishment, he said: severe. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: He took it severely. He said: Severe. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, So We seized him with a terrible punishment, he said: The terrible is the evil, and the Arabs say to someone who has been subjected to evil one after another: It has been afflicted upon him, and to someone who has been killed: You have been afflicted with polytheism. He said: And God was not satisfied that he should be drowned and tormented until he was settled in a permanent torment until he is sent to the Fire on the Day of Resurrection, meaning Pharaoh.
73:17: God Almighty says to those who associate others with Him: How can you fear, O people, a day that will turn children gray if you disbelieve in God and do not believe in Him? And He mentioned that this is the case in the reading of Abdullah bin Masoud. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, How can you guard yourself, if you disbelieve, against a Day that will turn the children gray-haired? He said: How can you guard yourself against a Day when you have disbelieved in it and do not believe in it? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: How will you guard yourselves if you disbelieve? He said: By God, no one who disbelieves in God will guard hisselves on that day. His saying: A Day that will turn children gray-haired means the Day of Resurrection, and children will turn gray from the intensity of its horror and distress. It was also narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement: A Day when He will turn children into grey-haired ones. Ibn Mas`ud used to say: “When the Day of Resurrection comes, our Lord will call upon the angel Adam and say: ‘O Adam, arise and send forth those who will be sent to Hellfire.’ Adam will say: ‘O Lord, I have no knowledge except what You have taught me.’ Then God will say to him: ‘Bring forth from every thousand nine hundred and ninety-nine,’ and they will be driven to Hellfire black and horned, blue and dark, and every newborn will turn grey there.” Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, A Day when the children will turn gray, he said: The young ones will turn gray from the distress of that day.
73:18: And His statement: The sky will be split by it. God Almighty says: The sky will be burdened by that day, cracked and split. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, The sky will be split by it, meaning: The sky will be split when the Most Merciful, the Majestic and Almighty, descends. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, broken by it, he said: burdened by it. Abu Hafs Al-Hiri told us, he said: Muammil told us, he said: Abu Mawdud told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement, The sky will be split by it, he said: It will be burdened and saddened on the Day of Resurrection. Ali bin Sahl told me, he said: Muammil told us, he said: Abu Mawdud Bahr bin Musa told us, he said: I heard Ibn Abi Ali say about this verse, then he mentioned something similar. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Al-Hussein told us, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Ikrimah: The sky is split by it. He said: It is heavy with it. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Abu Raja’ told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement, The sky will be split by it, he said: Heavy and burdened. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, The sky will be split open with it, meaning: it will be burdened with it that day. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, The sky will be split by it, he said: This is the Day of Resurrection, so He made the children gray, and the day the sky will be split, and he recited, When the sky is split (al-Infitar 82:1), and he said: All of this is on the Day of Resurrection. Abu Kurayb told us: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Abdullah bin Yahya, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The sky is split by it. He said: It is filled with it in the language of Abyssinia. Mahran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Ikrimah, and he did not hear it on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The sky is split open with it. He said: Filled with it. The sky is mentioned in this place because the Arabs make it masculine and feminine. Whoever makes it masculine directs it to the ceiling, as one says: This is the sky of the house for its ceiling. It may also be possible that they make it masculine because it is one of the nouns in which there is no difference between its feminine and masculine forms. Among the masculine forms is the poet’s saying: If He raised the sky to a people, we would join the sky with the clouds. And His statement: His promise was to be fulfilled, God Almighty says: What God promised to do was to be fulfilled, because He does not break His promise. And what He promised to do was to create it on the day when children will be gray-haired. He says: So beware of that day, O people, for it will inevitably happen.
73:19: He, the Most High, means by His statement: These verses in which He mentions the matter of the Resurrection and its horrors, and what He will do to the people of disbelief, are a reminder. He says: A lesson and admonition for whoever considers them and is admonished. So whoever wills, let him take to his Lord a way. He says: So whoever among creation wills, let him take a way to his Lord by believing in Him and working in obedience to Him. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Indeed, this is a reminder, meaning the Qur’an, so whoever wills may take to his Lord a way, by obeying God.
73:20: And his saying: Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand in prayer nearly two-thirds of the night. He is saying to his Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Your Lord, O Muhammad, knows that you stand in prayer nearly two-thirds of the night, half of it, or a third of it. The reciters differed in their recitation of this. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra recited it in the accusative case, and half of it and a third of it means: and less than half of it and a third of it. You were not able to do what was required of you of standing at night, so stand for less than two-thirds of the night and half of it and a third of it. Some of the reciters of Mecca and the majority of the reciters of Kufa recited it in the accusative case, meaning: you stand for less than two-thirds of the night, and you stand for half of it and a third of it. The correct thing to say about this is that they are two well-known readings with correct meanings, so whichever one the reader recites, he is correct. His saying: A group of those with you means the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who believed in God when the night prayer was imposed upon them. And his saying: And God determines the night and the day with hours and times. And His statement: He knew that you could not count it means: Your Lord knew, O people upon whom the night prayer was enjoined, that you would not be able to stand it. So He turned to you in forgiveness when you were unable and weak to do so, and He returned to you to make it easier for you. And similar to what we said about the meaning of His statement, that you will never count it, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us: Hisham told us, on the authority of Ibad bin Rashid, on the authority of Al-Hasan: He knew that you would not be able to count it means that you would not be able to bear it. Yaqoub told me, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Ibad bin Rashid told me, he said: I heard Al-Hasan say about His statement, that you will not be able to count it, he said: You will not be able to bear it. Ibn Hamid told us: Yaqub told us, on the authority of Ja`far, on the authority of Sa`id, He knew that you would not be able to count it means: that you would not be able to bear it. He said: Mahran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, He knew that you would not be able to count it. He said: That you would not be able to bear it. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘There are two qualities which no Muslim man can enumerate except that they will admit him into Paradise. They are easy, but few do them: glorify God ten times after every prayer, praise Him ten times, and magnify Him ten times.’ I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, counting them in his hand. He said: ‘That is one hundred and fifty on the tongue, and one thousand five hundred on the scale.’ And when he goes to bed, he glorifies, praises, and magnifies God one hundred times. He said: ‘That is one hundred on the tongue, and one thousand on the scale.’ Which of you does two thousand five hundred bad deeds in one day? They said: ‘How can we not count them?’ He said: ‘Satan comes to one of you while he is praying and says: Remember such and such, remember such and such, until he is distracted and perhaps he does not understand. Or Satan comes to him while he is in his bed and keeps making him sleep until he falls asleep.’” Abu Kuraib told us: Abu Naim told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: He knew that you would not be able to count it. The night prayer was prescribed for you. So recite what is easy for you of the Qur’an. His statement: So recite as much of the Qur’an as is easy for you means: Recite at night as much of the Qur’an as is easy for you in your prayers. This is an alleviation from God Almighty for His servants of the obligation that was imposed upon them in His statement: Stand [in prayer] during the night, except for a little - half of it or a little less. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’ Muhammad, he said: I said to Al-Hasan: O Abu Sa’id, what do you say about a man who has memorized the entire Qur’an by heart, but he does not stand up, but rather prays the obligatory prayers? He said: He uses the Qur’an as a pillow. May God curse that one. God said to the righteous servant: {And indeed, he was full of knowledge because We taught him and you were taught that which you did not know, neither you nor your fathers.} (Al-An’am 6:91), I said: O Abu Sa’id, God said: {So recite what is easy for you of the Qur’an.} He said: Yes, even if it is fifty verses. Abu Kuraib told us: Waki` told us, on the authority of Uthman al-Hamadani, on the authority of al-Suddi, regarding his statement, So recite as much of the Qur’an as is easy for you, he said: One hundred verses. He said: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Rabee’, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: Whoever recites one hundred verses in one night, the Qur’an will not dispute with him. He said: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ka’b, who said: Whoever recites one hundred verses in one night will be recorded among the worshippers. And His statement: He knows that among you will be sick and others traveling throughout the land seeking from the bounty of God means, Your Lord knows, O believers, that among you will be people of illness, whose illness has weakened them from praying at night. “And others traveling throughout the land” on journeys seek[ing] from the bounty of God in trade. They traveled to seek a livelihood, but it made them unable, so it also made them too weak to pray at night. And others fighting in the cause of God means, and still others among you will strive against the enemy, fighting them in support of the religion of God. So God had mercy on you and made it easy for you, and removed from you the obligation of praying at night. So recite what is easy for you from it means, So recite now that this has been made easy for you from the night in your prayers what is easy for you from the Qur’an. The ha in His statement from it is from the mention of the Qur’an. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: Then he informed us of the characteristics of the believers, and he said: “He knows that there will be among you those who are ill and others who travel throughout the land seeking from the bounty of God and others who fight in the cause of God. So recite what is easy of it.” He said: God made standing obligatory at the beginning of this surah, so the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions stood for a year until their feet swelled, and God held back its end for twelve months in the heavens, then He sent down the alleviation at the end of it, so standing at night became voluntary after it was obligatory. And establish prayer means: establish the obligatory prayers, which are the five daily prayers. And give zakat means: give the obligatory zakat on your wealth to those who are entitled to it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told me, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And establish prayer and give zakat. These are two obligatory duties, and no one has a license for them, so pay them to God, the Most High, the Most Great. His saying: And lend to God a good loan means: And spend in the way of God from your money. Ibn Zayd used to say about this: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And loan God a good loan, he said: The loan is the voluntary acts of worship other than zakat. And His statement: “And whatever good you send forth for yourselves - you will find it with God. It is better and greater in reward.” He says: Whatever you send forth, O believers, for yourselves in this world, of charity or spending in the way of God, or other spending in good ways, or doing acts of obedience to God, such as prayer, fasting, Hajj, or other good deeds seeking what is with God - you will find it with God on the Day of Resurrection in your place of return. It is better for you than what you sent forth in this world, and greater in reward. That is, its reward is greater than what you sent forth had you not sent forth. And seek forgiveness from God. God, the Most High, says: “And ask God to forgive your sins, and He will pardon you for them. “Indeed, God is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.” He says: God is Oft-Forgiving of the sins of whoever of His servants repents from their sins, and Oft-Forgiving to punish them for them after they have repented from them.
